I.A. No.23933 of 2025, second application under Section 430 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha
Sanhita, 2023/ 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure for suspension of sentence and grant of
bail to present appellant.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 21.04.2023 passed by the learned Second Additional Sessions Judge, Gadarwara, District- Narsinghpur (M.P.), in S.C. No.02 of 2021, whereby the present appellant has been convicted for offence punishable under Sections 366 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for five years with fine of Rs.5,000/-, under Section 376(2)(i) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten years with fine of Rs.5,000/-, under Section 376(2)(n) of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo R.I. for ten years with fine of Rs.10,000/- and under Section 5/6 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years with fine of Rs.10,000/- with default stipulations.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that the entire evidence available on record clearly indicates that the prosecutrix (PW-1) had voluntarily and with her consent accompanied the present appellant.

With regard to the age of the prosecutrix, it is submitted that the 2 CRA-1269-2024 testimony of Gopal (PW-3) and the documentary evidence relied upon by the prosecution are not worthy of reliance, inasmuch as there are apparent corrections and overwriting in the relevant register.
No plausible or satisfactory explanation for such corrections has been furnished by Gopal (PW-3).
It is further submitted that the medical examination of the prosecutrix does not support the allegation of forcible sexual intercourse, as there are no medical findings indicative of forceful rape.
In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, the prosecution case suffers from serious infirmities and the evidence on record does not support the allegations levelled against the appellant.
It is also submitted that the FSL report is negative and he has a good case on merits.
The final disposal of this appeal will take considerable time.
The appellant is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by the Court.
Therefore, it is prayed that the remaining jail sentence of present appellant may be suspended and he may be released on bail.

Per contra, learned counsel for State has opposed the prayer made by learned counsel for the appellant and prayed for rejection of application on the ground that prosecutrix has supported the Bhagwan Singh Vishwakarma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142294027/
1 story of the prosecution in toto.

sentences.text: She was 15 years old at the time of commission of the offence and in this regard, the learned trial Court has rightly believed the certificate (Exhibit- P/2) and scholar register (Exhibit-P/3) and found that at the time of commission of offence, prosecutrix was 15-17 years old and as she was minor at the time of incident, therefore, her consent does not assume importance.

It is also submitted that though the FSL report is negative but the 3 CRA-1269-2024 statement of the prosecutrix in respect of the offence committed by the present appellant is entirely believable and Gopal (PW-3) has given explanation for correction in the scholar register which is believable and the learned trial Court has rightly believed this evidence.
Hence, there is no ground to suspend the sentence of the appellant.

Having heard the rival contentions of learned counsel for the parties, perused the record and keeping in view the attending facts and circumstances of the case coupled with the fact that there is evidence against the present appellant but without commenting anything on the merits of the case,
at this stage, in the considered opinion of this Court, the present appellant is not entitled to get the benefit of suspension of sentence.
Accordingly, I.A. No.23933 of 2025 is rejected.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE julie Bhagwan Singh Vishwakarma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 2 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/142294027/
